title: Grateful Dead Live at Universal Amphitheatre on 1973-07-01
lineage: Matrix by Hunter Seamons using Final Cut Pro (FLAC > AIFF > Final Cut > AIFF CD tracking via Audacity > FLAC16 via xACT w/meta-tagging)
source: Matrix of SBD (shnid=127028): SBD -> Master Reel -> Sound Devices 744T (24bit/96k) and AUD (shnid=88528): Sony ECM-22P > Sony TC-770 > MAR > ?? [Dolby Encode] > R1

ai_review.summary: Excellent matrix recording with crystal‑clear guitar separation captures a soaring ’73 Dead show highlighted by a monster Truckin' > The Other One > Wharf Rat sequence.
ai_review.review: The Hunter Seamons matrix mix delivers outstanding sonic clarity, especially the distinct left/right guitar imaging that makes this set a pleasure to hear through headphones. Musically the concert is a high‑energy affair – a mellow first set gives way to a massive second set featuring a sublime China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider jam, a 25‑minute improvisational “Playing,” and an epic 41‑minute Truckin' > The Other One > Wharf Rat stretch. Overall the performance is vibrant and the recording quality makes it exceptionally listenable.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently high star ratings (average 4.6) and enthusiastic comments about both performance and sound quality indicate an exceptional show with excellent matrix recording.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Reviewers praise crystal‑clear channel separation, distinct guitars, and overall outstanding sonic fidelity; no mention of dropouts or muddiness.

standout_songs: China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
Truckin' > The Other One > Wharf Rat
show_quality.setlist_flow: Mellow first set with Half Step, Sugaree and China>Rider; second set launches into a 25‑minute exploratory jam followed by tight standards and the massive Truckin' > Other One > Wharf Rat marathon.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Guitar tones are noted as distinctly separated in the mix, delivering a thrilling listening experience.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil’s bass jumps into overdrive around 6:21 during the CC>IKYR jam, delivering a powerful “Phil JAM!” moment.
